objective.statement: Learn words that say how much: more, less, very and too much, and the word for movement.
successCriteria: I know più means more and meno means less.
I know molto and assai both mean very, and troppo means too much.
I can read directions such as meno mosso and ma non troppo.

explanation.text: These words change how much of something a direction asks for. Più and meno are opposites. Molto and assai both strengthen a word. Troppo warns against too much. Mosso means movement, and it is the word that più and meno most often meet.
“più” means more. “meno” means less. “molto” means very, or much. “troppo” means too much.

Più mosso means with more movement, so a little faster; meno mosso means with less movement, so slower. Non troppo means not too much, and ma non troppo means but not too much. Molto vivace means very lively, and allegro assai means very quick.

steps: Look at the words above the first bar: meno mosso.
Meno means less and mosso means movement, so the music should move less: a little slower.
The words ask for a change of feeling, not a new tune.

The terms are the reference list printed for Grade 2 (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q2: no authoritative list is published, so a qualified teacher must approve the list and its grade placement, Q38). “Più mosso” is a standard direction not printed in the list; it is the opposite of the printed “meno mosso”, and it is flagged for the teacher.
